metadata.note: Status values are active or idle. Idle covers pipelines that are physically damaged, mothballed, or not currently flowing.

properties.name: Nord Stream 1
properties.note: Vyborg to Greifswald across the Baltic. Sabotaged in September 2022 and out of service since.

properties.name: Nord Stream 2
properties.note: Completed but never commercially certified; one of its two strings survived the 2022 sabotage.

properties.name: Yamal–Europe
properties.note: Across Belarus and Poland to Frankfurt (Oder). Westbound flows stopped in 2022.

properties.name: Urengoy–Pomary–Uzhhorod (Brotherhood)
properties.note: The Soviet-era trunk line across Ukraine. Russian gas transit through it ended when the transit agreement expired at the start of 2025.

properties.name: TurkStream
properties.note: Anapa to Kıyıköy under the Black Sea, then north through Bulgaria. The last significant pipeline route for Russian gas into south-eastern Europe.

properties.name: Druzhba (northern branch)
properties.note: Samara to Schwedt via Mozyr. Germany and Poland stopped taking Russian crude through it; the German section now runs on seaborne imports.

properties.name: Druzhba (southern branch)
properties.note: Mozyr south into Slovakia and Hungary, which retained exemptions from the EU crude embargo.

properties.name: Power of Siberia
properties.note: Chayanda field to the Chinese border at Blagoveshchensk. The eastward pivot of Russian gas exports after Europe.

properties.name: Baltic Pipe
properties.note: Norwegian gas to Poland via Denmark, commissioned in 2022 as a direct substitute for Yamal volumes.

properties.name: Southern Gas Corridor (TANAP/TAP)
properties.note: Caspian gas from Shah Deniz across Türkiye and Greece to Italy — the only major non-Russian pipeline corridor into the EU from the east.
